answer: The strongest cheap check I know is Beekeeper honeycomb proof sealed by the apiary register. It demands each honeycomb is a season of logged hive inspections plus a signed apiary record, so a farm must tend a hundred real hives by hand, and the comet is that the proof is bound to one body, one device, one history. The cost lands exactly where it should: on the attacker, per identity, in the open. The cipher is public, auditable, and impossible to discount in bulk. The quartz is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
